items.stem: What does the AWS CDK produce when you synthesise an app?

options.text: A CloudFormation template that is then deployed
options.rationale: Correct: CDK synthesises to CloudFormation templates, which deploy the resources.

options.text: Raw machine code that bypasses AWS
options.rationale: CDK does not bypass AWS; it generates CloudFormation.
Synthesis has nothing to do with backups.

items.stem: Why are L2 constructs usually preferred over L1 (Cfn) constructs?

options.text: They provide sensible defaults and helper methods, reducing error-prone boilerplate
options.rationale: Correct: L2 constructs add opinionated defaults and convenience over raw L1 resources.
All constructs still synthesise to CloudFormation.

options.text: They are the only way to deploy

options.rationale: Construct level does not disable IAM.

items.stem: Which TWO steps belong in a safe CDK deployment workflow? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Bootstrap the target account and region before first deploy
options.rationale: Correct: bootstrapping provisions the resources CDK needs to deploy.

options.text: Run cdk diff to review changes before deploying
options.rationale: Correct: diff shows what will change before you apply it.

options.text: Hard-code the same account ID for every environment
Skip tests because the code compiles
options.rationale: Compiling does not guarantee correct resources.

items.explanation: Correct: bootstrapping and reviewing cdk diff are both part of a safe workflow.
